articles.title: Cognitive abilities predict how well people manage their emotional responses
articles.summary: A recent study reveals that accumulated life knowledge helps adults manage their emotions across various situations, while fast mental processing speed is primarily linked to successfully reducing negative feelings like sadness and disgust.

articles.title: The link between vitamin intake and depression largely vanishes when factoring in lifestyle
articles.summary: While higher vitamin intake is often linked to better mental health, a new study reveals that this relationship mostly disappears once socioeconomic status, daily habits, and overall physical health are taken into account.

articles.title: ADHD medication helps children focus by stabilizing brain networks, new study suggests
articles.summary: A common ADHD medication helps children focus by stabilizing how different regions of the brain communicate, reducing the rapid shifts in neural connections that often lead to distraction.

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary: A simple change in posture may subtly affect how people feel and make decisions. Participants who sat upright reported greater feelings of pride and took more successful risks in a virtual balloon game than those who hunched over. Most did not realize researchers had influenced their posture, helping rule out the possibility that they were merely responding to expectations. The results suggest workplace ergonomics could influence more than physical comfort.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary: A group of brain cells called orexin neurons appears to help us keep working when reaching a reward becomes increasingly difficult. Blocking their activity weakened motivation in rats, pointing to a possible new target for understanding why people sometimes struggle to sustain goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Single people who pursue novel activities report better psychological health, study finds
articles.summary: Being single offers a unique chance for personal growth. A recent psychology study suggests that single adults who view their relationship status as an opportunity to try new things experience greater daily well-being and less anxiety.

articles.title: Social anxiety and depression appear to change the way we process feedback
articles.summary: A new study reveals how social anxiety and depression distort the way people update their self-beliefs in response to feedback. While social anxiety amplifies negative judgments about competence, depression makes it difficult to accept positive feedback entirely.

articles.title: A Long-Run Persistence Theory for AI Systems under the Redundancy-Adjusted Artificial Age Score (AAS)
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly expected to operate over repeated cycles of interaction, adaptation, and update rather than through isolated one-shot outputs. This raises a fundamental theoretical question: can an AI system persist indefinitely without incurring unbounded structural aging? This paper develops a long-run persistence framework for AI systems based on the redundancy-adjusted Artificial Age Score (AAS). The model extends AAS from a static evaluative measure into a cycle-level functional that generates an age sequence

articles.title: The LLM Proposes, the Executive Disposes: A Self-Verifying Agent Instrument that Dissociates Commitment Drift from Binding Drift in Long-Horizon Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How do you verify a long-horizon agent when its own state and self-reports are exactly what you cannot trust? We present an agent instrument built so that verification is structural rather than post-hoc. A deterministic Executive owns all belief; a language model may only file typed proposals, and a claim is admitted only when a prediction pre-registered before acting is matched against observation by code. articles.title: FinProBench: Evaluating Financial AI Agents with Role-Grounded Rubrics Derived from Professional Deliverables
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating financial AI agents requires criteria aligned with real professional work. Existing rubric methods typically derive criteria from task prompts or model outputs, overlooking tacit standards visible only in practitioner deliverables. We introduce FinProBench, a benchmark for professional financial tasks, and Role-Grounded Rubric Construction (RGRC), a reusable pipeline that derives rubrics from deliverables produced by practitioners in the same role. articles.title: Gratitude makes people more helpful, but it doesn’t overcome the bystander effect
articles.summary: A new study published in Cognition and Emotion indicates that while gratitude boosts your overall willingness to help someone in need, it doesn't overcome the bystander effect. Even grateful people hesitate when a crowd is present.
